ADA-S2-2026.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care. 2026;49(Suppl 1):S27–S49.
ADA-S2-2026.supports: Diagnostic cut-offs: A1C 6.5% or above; fasting plasma glucose 126 mg/dL or above; random glucose with classic symptoms. Prediabetes: A1C 5.7–6.4%, fasting glucose 100–125 mg/dL. Confirmatory testing is required without unequivocal hyperglycaemia.

ADA-S6-2026.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care. 2026;49(Suppl 1):S132–S149.
ADA-S6-2026.supports: Hypoglycaemia levels: level 1 below 70 and at or above 54 mg/dL; level 2 below 54 mg/dL; level 3 defined by needing assistance. Written for people with diabetes.

ISPAD-2024.citation: Haller MJ, Bell KJ, Besser REJ, et al. ISPAD Clinical Practice Consensus Guidelines 2024: Screening, Staging, and Strategies to Preserve Beta-Cell Function in Children and Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes. Horm Res Paediatr. 2024;97(6):529–545.
ISPAD-2024.supports: Stage 1: two or more islet autoantibodies confirmed on two samples, normal glucose, no symptoms. Stage 2: the same with dysglycaemia. Stage 3: meets diagnostic criteria, with or without symptoms. A single autoantibody carries roughly a 15% risk of stage 3 within 15 years; two or more, 80% to over 90%.

INSEL-2015.citation: Insel RA, Dunne JL, Atkinson MA, et al. Staging Presymptomatic Type 1 Diabetes: A Scientific Statement of JDRF, the Endocrine Society, and the American Diabetes Association. Diabetes Care. 2015;38(10):1964–1974.
INSEL-2015.supports: The three-stage classification of presymptomatic type 1 diabetes.

ENDOTEXT-T1D.citation: Pathogenesis of Type 1 Diabetes. In: Endotext. MDText.com, Inc.
ENDOTEXT-T1D.supports: About 85% of people who develop type 1 diabetes have no family history. US prevalence by age 20 is about 0.3% (1 in 300), against about 5% (1 in 20) with an affected relative. Figures are from US non-Hispanic white youth.

CDC-DKA.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Diabetic Ketoacidosis.
CDC-DKA.supports: DKA signs: great thirst, frequent urination, fast deep breathing, fruity-smelling breath, nausea and vomiting, stomach pain, tiredness. It can be the first sign of undiagnosed diabetes. Severe symptoms can appear quickly; it is an emergency.

PHILHEALTH-KONSULTA.citation: Philippine Health Insurance Corporation. Annex B: Konsulta Benefit Table. PhilHealth Circular 2024-0013.
PHILHEALTH-KONSULTA.supports: The primary care package lists fasting blood sugar, oral glucose tolerance test and HbA1c among its laboratory examinations, as needed and on the primary care team's assessment. Renamed YAKAP in 2025. A test may be done at a partner laboratory rather than on site.

DOH-NHFR.citation: Department of Health, Republic of the Philippines. National Health Facility Registry.
DOH-NHFR.supports: The official master list of health facilities. Located but NOT queried facility by facility in this build.
